title: trace pipeline breadcrumbs scratchpad
content:
Quick context:
- Noticed intermittent TRACE volume drop for user-facing services (frontend->api proxy) around 2025-02-17 03:10-03:25 UTC.
- Metrics (trace_rate_total) down ~70% for 15m window, Prometheus scrape still up for other exporters.
- Logs show Otel-Collector restarting / export failures, Fluent Bit occasionally returning 401 from Loki.
- Suspect: recent telemetry config change in PR#45 (sampler/attribute filter) or upstream network auth change.

What I saw (timeline / breadcrumbs):
- 03:09 UTC: SLO alert triggered (trace ingestion drop). Dashboards show span count drop for api-proxy service.
- 03:11 UTC: First pager; I ssh'd into bastion and kubectl port-forwarded otel-collector to local 4317 to test connectivity.
- 03:12 UTC: otel-collector logs: "error exporting traces: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = \"transport: authentication handshake failed\""
- 03:14 UTC: Fluent Bit logs: "[error] HTTP status=401 Unauthorized, url=https://loki.prod.internal/loki/api/v1/push" (batch dropped)
- 03:16 UTC: Restarted otel-collector (kubectl rollout restart deployment/otel-collector -n observability) — partial recovery, then drop again at 03:22.

Commands I ran (copy/paste):
$ kubectl get pods -n observability -o wide
NAME                                 READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE   IP\notel-collector-78d9f7c4c-5xj2z      1/1     Running   12         7d    10.10.3.12
fluent-bit-6k9fp                     1/1     Running   0          3d    10.10.3.45

$ kubectl logs deployment/otel-collector -n observability --since=30m | grep -i error -A2 -B2
2025-02-17T03:12:14Z    otelcol    exporting failed: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = \"transport: authentication handshake failed: tls: certificate signed by unknown authority\"
2025-02-17T03:12:14Z    otelcol    retrying in 3s

$ curl -s -v --insecure https://loki.prod.internal/loki/api/v1/push -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n"
401

$ kubectl exec -n observability -it otel-collector-78d9f7c4c-5xj2z -- /bin/sh -c "apk add --no-cache curl; curl -v telnet://upstream-telemetry:4317"
(used telnet to verify port reachable)

What I tried (mitigations):
- Restarted otel-collector and fluent-bit pods (kubectl rollout restart) — temporary partial recoveries.
- Rolled back PR#45 in a canary namespace to compare behaviour (no immediate data drop there).
- Increased otel-collector exporter TLS debug level and collected logs.
- Captured tcpdump on otel-collector pod host to check TLS handshake (saw RSTs occasionally).
- Temporarily set Fluent Bit output to buffer and file to avoid immediate drops for 20m window.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) TLS/certificate trust change on upstream telemetry lane (rotated certs or CA not trusted by new image). Error "certificate signed by unknown authority" matches.
2) Auth token rotation for Loki (401) — maybe a secret expired or service account token not mounted/renewed.
3) New attribute filter/sampling config in PR#45 inadvertently changed service.name or dropped key attribute used by routing, causing exporter to reject (policy mismatch).
4) Network flakiness / NAT gateway hit connection limits causing half-open handshakes.

Evidence supporting #1:
- otel-collector explicit TLS error.
- Upstream telemetry (receiver) team reported a cert rotation around 2025-02-17 02:50 UTC (check PR/ops note).
- Canary namespace with older image/config did not show the drop.

Evidence supporting #2:
- Fluent Bit 401s correspond to timestamps of token rotation job executed 2025-02-17 02:45 UTC (see RED-1123 notes).
- Some logs show "unauthorized" responses from Loki but not consistently, which suggests token caching/refresh delay.

Open checks to do (next):
- Verify certs on upstream endpoint: openssl s_client -connect upstream-telemetry:4317 -showcerts (from within cluster).
- Inspect secret mounts in otel-collector pod: kubectl describe pod -n observability otel-collector-78d9f7c4c-5xj2z (look for cert, caBundle, token).
- Confirm whether the telemetry upstream rotated CA; drop-in call with infra/telemetry team (Marco).
- Check Kubernetes events for secret update/recreate around 02:40-03:00 UTC.
- Rotate to a trusted CA bundle in otel-collector as a quick test (apply configmap with caBundle).

Repro steps (minimal):
1) In cluster, run: kubectl run -n test-obs -it --rm debug --image=alpine -- sh
2) apk add --no-cache openssl curl
3) openssl s_client -connect upstream-telemetry:4317 -showcerts -verify 5
4) curl -v --cacert /path/to/bundled-ca https://loki.prod.internal/loki/api/v1/push

Notes to self / loose TODOs:
- If cert rotation confirmed, coordinate a rolling restart of otel-collector with updated CA bundle; communicate to SRE and telemetry upstream.
- Add alert for otel_exporter_tls_errors (simple counter) so next time we get more actionable page.
- Revisit PR#45 sampler change; add integration test that runs a canary against upstream to ensure attributes used for routing remain intact.
- Add a runbook snippet: \"If otel-collector: certificate signed by unknown authority -> check secret CA, check upstream CA rotation, check otel image trust store\".
- Follow up: ask infra to confirm if NAT gateway logs show connection RST spikes around the window.

Last raw snippets I saved (for debugging paste):
- otel log sample:
2025-02-17T03:12:14Z otelcol exporter.go:54: exporting failed: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = \"transport: authentication handshake failed: tls: certificate signed by unknown authority\"

- fluent-bit sample:
[2025/02/17 03:12:35] [error] [http_client] server returned status=401

- tcpdump snippet (base64 chunked captured): saved to /tmp/trace-dump-20250217.pcap (on bastion).

Slack notes: pinged @Marco Li in #observability at 03:19 UTC, dropped a short summary and link to RED-1123 (see linked_artifacts).

If I lose context (notes for future me):
- Start with exporter TLS error — most likely cause. Check certs, CA bundles, secret mounts. Then look at token rotation for Loki.
- Record any change in ingestion rate vs span count correlation to confirm if only traces affected or metrics/logs as well.

End of scratchpad. Will update after the call with infra and telemetry teams.
